atoms.text: Oscar has been given a homework project titled trees. He is going to do an internet search to find out what kind of trees are found in the UK.

instruction.text: How should Oscar carry out his internet research? Sort the steps.

atoms.text: 1. Think of suitable search words for the topic.
atoms.sound: Think of suitable search words for the topic

atoms.text: 2. Open the search engine and enter the search.
atoms.sound: Open the search engine and enter the search.

atoms.text: 3. Read through the list of websites.
atoms.sound: Read through the list of websites

atoms.text: 5. View texts, videos or photos relevant to the topic.
atoms.sound: View texts, videos or photos relevant to the topic

atoms.text: 6. Make relevant notes and write down the link to the website.
atoms.sound: Make relevant notes and write down the link to the website

instruction.text: In order to find relevant information on the internet as quickly as possible, Oscar should know a few tips. Fill in the gaps for Oscar.

atoms.b:
Search Tips:
1. Make your search as ((specific)) as possible.
2. Enter ((several)) relevant search terms.
3. Pay attention to your ((spelling)).

instruction.text: Are these sensible search terms for Oscar’s UK trees research? Drag them into the correct groups.
Write the word tree in the search bar.

atoms.text: When searching tree, the search engine found almost 47 million results. There are so many results because the search term was very general.

instruction.text: Select the search tip that fixes this problem.
Write trees in the UK in the search bar.
How many search results has the search engine found now? Select the correct answer.

feedback.end: Correct. With several relevant search terms, there are fewer results. This search is better because it is more specific.
